# Audit — skills/objectstack-pm-dispatch (published, read-only)

Pinned ref: objectstack `origin/main` = `a59f78d`. Verified the working file is byte-identical
to the pinned blob (`git show a59f78d:skills/objectstack-pm-dispatch/SKILL.md | md5sum` ==
`md5sum` of the checkout copy = `3948bdb8c73dba124ebc2e61a832d1db`). All spans below are at
that ref. Local `HEAD` is `a39b02a`, but `git diff a59f78d HEAD -- skills/` is empty.

Because the package contains zero `ts`/`tsx` fences, dimension E's type-check sweep has no

## The customer's five real decision points

Derived from what a single-repo ObjectStack **app project** with no internal tooling can act
on, not from the doc's own headings:

1. Provision the three labels and read them as a state machine (134-170, 151-159).
2. Claim an issue so two agents cannot collide (320-343, 371-375).
3. Compose a dispatch prompt with a binding operating template (377-415, 729-891).
4. Review the returned PR **against GitHub** and land it (529-564).
5. Decide what to escalate versus decide under a veto window (565-595, 648-706).

Everything measured below as monorepo lore changes none of these five.

---

## Findings

### PMD-A-01 · TRIGGER PRECISION · `skills/objectstack-pm-dispatch/SKILL.md:10-14`
**Evidence.** The frontmatter advertises a second, unrelated job: "Ships the developer-agent
operating template … **and the upstream-reporting procedure for platform defects an app
project finds**. Use when asked to … **or to report a platform bug found while building an
app.**" A customer agent that trips over a platform defect while authoring metadata loads
**14,549 tokens** to reach the 882-token §"Upstream reporting" (916-986), of which ~600 restates
`skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md:59-70` (see PMD-C-01). `skills/README.md`'s index row is
generated from this same description (the `BEGIN GENERATED: skills` HTML-comment marker, README:29-45), so
the mis-routing is mirrored into the catalog automatically.
**Proposal.** `MOVE-TO skills/objectstack-platform` (the ~250 tokens of unique procedure) and
delete both the "Ships … upstream-reporting procedure" clause and the "or to report a platform
bug" trigger; regenerate README via `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec gen:skill-docs`.
**Delta.** −30 (frontmatter only; the section itself is counted in PMD-C-01).
**Gate.** ① Yes — it decides *which package a customer loads* for a bug report. ② Yes, deletion.
③ N/A (frontmatter). **Confidence** HIGH. **Human floor** YES (changes a published trigger).

### PMD-A-02 · TRIGGER PRECISION · `skills/README.md:94-110`
**Evidence.** "Cross-skill routing" carries 4 bullets, all pairs of *domain* skills
(data/automation, automation/ui, formula, platform/data). Nothing routes between the two
`process` skills, and nothing tells an app author when a process skill applies at all. Both
process packages sit in the generated index (README:44-45) with no disambiguation, and their
descriptions overlap on the word "process" and on escalation-to-owner language
(`objectstack-upgrade` frontmatter: "work the semantic residue … to a decision with the
project's owner").
**Proposal.** `ADD` one routing bullet ("Delivery loop vs protocol upgrade …"). Payment must
come from README itself; the generated index block (29-45) is generator-owned and cannot pay.
**Delta.** +25 unpaid — flagged, not recommended without a maintainer ruling.
**Gate.** ① Yes. ② No. ③ Bullet in an existing list. **Confidence** MED. **Human floor** no.

### PMD-B-01 · STRUCTURE · whole file (1-1086)
**Evidence.** One 14,549-token file with **no progressive disclosure at all**. Two blocks are
needed only at a specific moment yet are paid in every session: the developer-agent template
(729-891, **2,376 tok**) is a verbatim paste-block consumed only when a dispatch is actually
composed, and §"Upstream reporting" (916-986, **882 tok**) is a different job entirely.
`skills/README.md:57-64` lists `rules/` as an available optional directory for any skill; the
"process skill carries `SKILL.md` alone" sentence (README:66-69) is scoped to `references/`
("`gen:skill-refs` only visits skills listed in its `SKILL_MAP`"), so it does not block a
`rules/` split.
**Proposal.** `MOVE-TO rules/dev-template.md` (the paste-block, linked from §5) and — with
PMD-C-01 — out of the package for upstream reporting.
**Delta.** −3,258 from the always-loaded entry file (a new `rules/` file takes its own ceiling).
**Gate.** ① Yes — it decides what a PM pays before it has dispatched anything. ② Partly
(relocation, not deletion). ③ Yes, the template stays a construct. **Confidence** HIGH.
**Human floor** YES (restructures files; new ratchet ceiling).

### PMD-B-02 · STRUCTURE · `SKILL.md:869-882` **and** `894-908`
**Evidence.** The same 8-key report schema is printed twice, 12 lines apart, differing only in
placeholder-vs-literal values (`"issue": N` vs `"issue": 123`; `"pr": "URL or null"` vs
`"pr": "https://github.com/acme/hotcrm/pull/456 | null"`). Only 909-914 adds new rules
("`open_questions` must be non-empty when `status` is `needs_decision`"; "`out_of_scope_findings`
should already be filed …").
**Proposal.** `DELETE` the fence at 894-908; keep 909-914 as a note under the template.
**Delta.** −115. **Gate.** ① No decision is changed by the second copy. ② Yes. ③ Construct
preserved. **Confidence** HIGH. **Human floor** no.

### PMD-B-03 · DENSITY · `SKILL.md:346-357` (232 tok), duplicated in substance at `884-888` (73 tok)
**Evidence.** The sanitizer trap is taught twice. 346-357 spends 12 lines on measured
specimens — "the `dev-report` HTML-comment marker came back as *nothing at all*, `expected N to be 19` came
back as `expected  to be 19`, `git log -- PATH` came back as `git log -- `" — plus three
lines on why this differs from step 0's truncation shape. The actionable rules are 359-365
("Write literal angle brackets as HTML entities … read it back"), and 884-888 restates the
whole trap inside the pasted template for the dev.
**Proposal.** `DELETE 346-357`, replacing with one clause on 359 ("measured: code spans are not
protection — an HTML comment came back empty").
**Delta.** −200. **Gate.** ① No — the rule at 359-365 already changes the decision; the
specimens change nothing. ② Yes. ③ Rules survive as a construct. **Confidence** HIGH.
**Human floor** no.

### PMD-C-01 · CROSS-PACKAGE REDUNDANCY · `SKILL.md:916-986` (882 tok) vs `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md:59-70`
**Evidence — both locations quoted.**
*pm-dispatch:918-924* — "The temptation is to make the app tolerate it and move on. Do not. A
workaround in the app hides the defect from the people who can fix it, ships a second source of
truth to every future author, and outlives the upstream fix by years."
*platform:59-61* — "**Business features belong in the app; capability belongs in the platform.**
A missing default, a wrong diagnostic, a shape the spec refuses — the fix is upstream. Raise it
there; do not compensate for it here."
*pm-dispatch:974-985* — park via `Blocked-by:` or "pin the current upstream version with the
unblock condition written down … A pin with no recorded unblock condition is a workaround with
better manners"; "**'We worked around it' is never a resolution**".
*platform:62-69* — "**A platform defect means waiting for the platform fix.** No defensive
coding, no shape tolerance … Record the block against the platform issue so it is
machine-visible; before resuming, confirm the version you **pin** carries the fix (merged
upstream ≠ present on your pin) and re-run the defect's own reproduction."
**Which anchor survives.** `objectstack-platform` — it is the app-bootstrap package every app
project loads to stand the project up, it already carries the doctrine, and it is where an
agent already is when it hits the defect. The genuinely unique residue in pm-dispatch is ~250
tokens: derive the upstream repo from the dependency's `package.json` `repository` (925-930);
minimal repro + pinned versions + cite the contract (944-958); **file as a guest — never apply
the upstream's queue labels, never assign, never add to their board** (959-971).
**Proposal.** `MOVE-TO skills/objectstack-platform` (~250 tok of residue), `DELETE` the rest.
**Delta.** −882 here (+~250 there).
**Gate.** ① Yes — it decides which package owns the doctrine. ② Yes, mostly deletion. ③ The
survivor is a 3-bullet checklist. **Confidence** HIGH on the overlap, MED on the exact split.
**Human floor** YES (moves published capability text across packages).

### PMD-D-01 · DENSITY / MONOREPO · `SKILL.md:192-217` (433 tok)
**Evidence.** "**Why the sweep is a disjunction and not one 'unlabeled' filter.**" followed by
two "standing producers" that exist only here: "**Cross-seat transfer tickets** (the handing-off
side applies the queue label as part of the transfer) and tickets filed mechanically by a
**steward automation** both carry `pm:queue` on arrival, while a **single-producer discipline for
classification labels** forbids those same producers from applying one", plus the anecdote "a
project that had published exactly that rule hours earlier still produced such a card the same
day". "Seat", "steward automation", "lane" (180) and "protocol posts" (215) are used as defined
terms and are defined nowhere in the package; an app project has none of them.
**Proposal.** `REWRITE-AS-CONSTRUCT` — keep the 3-item disjunct list (179-191), fold the ⚠️
scoping caution (209-217) to one line and the ⏳ `updated_at` floor (219-225) to one line, drop
the producers and the anecdote.
**Delta.** −380. **Gate.** ① No — the customer either runs the predicate or (per the ⚠️ at
209-214) must not; the rationale changes neither. ② Yes. ③ Yes, list survives.
**Confidence** HIGH. **Human floor** no.

### PMD-D-02 · DENSITY · `SKILL.md:507-528` (357 tok)
**Evidence.** The section states the number is not transferable and then prints it anyway:
"Two same-day samples from this repo's loop show why **no single number can be inherited**: four
text-only documentation cards landed at 93 / 96 / ~95 / ~110 min, while four mixed cards from
the same day spanned ~64 min to ~2 h 50 min (the two long ones waiting on CI). Eight cards, one
day, one toolchain …". The decision-changing content is the rule at 507-512 + 516-518.
**Proposal.** `REWRITE-AS-CONSTRUCT` — "A silence threshold is a collection boundary, not a
verdict of death. Before concluding a dispatched agent is dead, require one of: a direct status
query showing it dead, the host reporting the session stopped, or silence past a completion
baseline **you measured in your own project**."
**Delta.** −290. **Gate.** ① No — the data is explicitly disclaimed as non-inheritable.
② Yes. ③ Yes. **Confidence** HIGH. **Human floor** no.

### PMD-D-03 · DENSITY · `SKILL.md:483-495` (of the 404-tok block 483-506)
**Evidence.** "Measured three times in one day on this loop: a scheduled message **still
delivered after its timer had been cancelled**, carrying text two rounds out of date. One of
them read 'no branch and no report ⇒ judge the agent unreliable and dispatch a fresh one'; by
delivery time that agent had opened a PR which was already reviewed and accepted …". The two
rules that follow (496-506: open every check-in with "idempotent — re-read the state before
acting"; state criteria never conclusions; "cancellation is not a guarantee of non-delivery")
are general and genuinely decision-changing, and already carry the surprising fact.
**Proposal.** `DELETE 483-495`; keep 496-506 intact.
**Delta.** −170. **Gate.** ① No — 496-506 already changes the decision. ② Yes. ③ The two rules
are the construct. **Confidence** MED (the anecdote is the only place the cancelled-timer fact
is *shown*; it is however *stated* at 505-506). **Human floor** no.

### PMD-D-04 · DENSITY · `SKILL.md:654-706` (861 tok) vs `826-857` (574 tok)
**Evidence.** The four-axis frame is stated twice in one file, in near-identical wording. PM-side
axis ④: "**Startup scope discipline.** Do not grow the declared surface while the core is still
forming. 'We already shipped it' earns nothing: a **shipped-but-unconsumed capability gets no
sunk-cost exemption**." Template copy: "Startup scope discipline — do not grow the declared
surface: a shipped-but-unconsumed capability gets no sunk-cost exemption." The weight and
ranking rules are likewise duplicated ("Axis ② carries the highest weight — at least 50%",
697-706, vs "Long-term soundness carries the highest weight, at least 50%", 853-857). The
template copy must stay verbatim (it is pasted into a zero-context prompt).
**Proposal.** `REWRITE-AS-CONSTRUCT` the PM-side copy as a 4-row table (axis · question ·
evidence standard) plus the ranking/weight rule, pointing at the template block for full wording.
**Delta.** −450. **Gate.** ① No new decision from the second full prose copy. ② Partly. ③ Yes —
a table replaces prose. **Confidence** MED. **Human floor** no (no semantics removed).

### PMD-E-01 · MONOREPO ASSUMPTION · `SKILL.md:179-217`
**Evidence.** Disjuncts 2 and 3 are keyed on a "**classification label**" — "none of the labels
your project reads as 'already routed' (area, component, owning team, **lane**)". This is the
monorepo's `domain:*` lane vocabulary (`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md:36` runs seats by
`DOMAIN` lane). The package's own ⚠️ at 209-214 makes the disjuncts **self-disabling** where
the label does not exist: "Where it does not exist, its absence is universal, so the disjunct
matches every open queue card in that repository and the sweep becomes its own noise source."
A customer app project has no classification labels, so 2 of the 3 disjuncts and their entire
rationale are **inert by construction** — the customer pays 433 tokens (PMD-D-01) to learn a
predicate it must not run.
**Proposal.** Folded into PMD-D-01; additionally define or drop "seat"/"lane"/"steward
automation"/"protocol posts".
**Delta.** counted in PMD-D-01. **Confidence** HIGH. **Human floor** no.

### PMD-E-02 · MONOREPO ASSUMPTION · `SKILL.md:416-452` (565 tok)
**Evidence.** "#### One semantics, N independent implementations". Its own applicability clause
names the platform's problem, not an app's: "that rule is implemented **more than once**, by
**compilers or evaluators that share no code**. **Query filters, expression languages,
permission predicates and serialization formats** all tend to grow this shape as a project adds
backends." An ObjectStack **app project** consumes one compiled query/expression surface from
`@objectstack/spec`; it authors no compiler and has no second evaluator to enumerate. The two
maintenance disciplines that follow (440-452, 201 tok — "The inventory is maintained by PR",
"Re-verify before pasting", frozen surfaces stay listed) are entirely about owning such an
inventory.
**Proposal.** `RETIRE-SURFACE` from the published package (it belongs to the internal corpus,
outside the published boundary).
**Delta.** −565. **Gate.** ① Changes no decision an app project can make. ② Yes, deletion.
③ N/A. **Confidence** HIGH. **Human floor** YES (removes published capability text).

### PMD-E-03 · MONOREPO ASSUMPTION · `SKILL.md:591-611` (398 tok) + `612-618` (110 tok)
**Evidence.** Two of the six "named non-escalation classes" are platform-governance shapes.
591-592: "**A declaration silently dropped on a new arm, when a sibling arm already has a
ruling.** When a **declared key** is silently ignored on **one arm of a component** and an
earlier ruling already made that same key a **loud authoring error** on a sibling arm, the new
arm **joins the existing rejection set by default**" — this is the enforce-or-remove /
`declared = enforced` machinery of this repo's spec work (the same vocabulary drives the
`spec-property-retirement` internal playbook), and an app project authoring metadata against a
fixed published spec has no "arm of a component" carrying declarations. 612-618: "**Two
implementations of one operation** … the side that already carries the **governance** —
authorization gates, user consent, de-duplication, audit trail — is the **default survivor**"
— a platform-runtime concern.
**Proposal.** `DELETE` both bullets; keep "Restore-invariant fixes", "Sequencing and dependency
ordering", "Verification strategy", and the `needs_decision`-relay bullet.
**Delta.** −508. **Gate.** ① No decision an app PM makes. ② Yes. ③ N/A. **Confidence** HIGH.
**Human floor** YES.

### PMD-E-04 · MONOREPO ASSUMPTION · `SKILL.md:769-786` (290 tok)
**Evidence.** Four correctness properties of a container-wide verification lock — "ONE shared
heavy-verify lock per container, so every agent contends on the same file"; "The acquisition
budget fits inside a SINGLE foreground tool call"; "A queue timeout is distinguishable from the
wrapped command's own failure"; "Hold duration is observable". This is the design spec of this
repo's `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` (the internal `os-dev` agent calls it by path). The
published text concedes the customer has none: "**The MECHANISM is the host project's** (its
wrapper, its lock path, its budget — put it in the conventions file)". A customer standing up
the loop on day one therefore reads 290 tokens instructing it to *build lock infrastructure*
before it may dispatch.
**Proposal.** `REWRITE-AS-CONSTRUCT` — one line: "Serialize build/test through a single
container-wide lock; queueing is normal, queueing with no end in sight is a finding — report it
naming the holder."
**Delta.** −250. **Gate.** ① The 4 properties change no decision for a project with no wrapper.
② Yes. ③ Yes. **Confidence** HIGH. **Human floor** YES (removes published guidance).

### PMD-E-05 · MONOREPO ASSUMPTION · `SKILL.md:987-1033` (656 tok)
**Evidence.** The whole section presupposes ≥2 repositories — which Configuration (79-117)
declares the *non-default* case ("With no config the loop runs against the current repository:
it is the only shard *and* the backlog", 60-61) — plus a **shard registry issue**: "**Shard
ownership is registered, never assumed.** A registry issue in the backlog repository records
which session owns which shard. A PM taking over a shard comments there as its FIRST action,
and again when handing off." That is this monorepo's `pm:seat` seat-post protocol
(`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` state model row: "`pm:seat` 座位登记贴 —— 协议载体") under
another name. Its own conclusion is one line: "**Multiple PMs on the same queue: prohibited.**"
**Proposal.** `REWRITE-AS-CONSTRUCT` — one Guardrails bullet: "One PM per queue. Scale with
`batch` / `mode:cloud`, never a second scheduler; a second PM takes a whole other repository as
its shard and never claims outside it."
**Delta.** −580. **Gate.** ① For the documented default (single repo) it changes nothing.
② Yes. ③ Yes. **Confidence** HIGH. **Human floor** YES.

### PMD-E-06 · MONOREPO ASSUMPTION (minor) · `SKILL.md:553-556`
**Evidence.** The landing path leads with the merge-queue case — "where a **merge queue**
exists, mark the PR ready and add it to the queue once every check is green (the queue rebuilds
against the current default branch, which is the sanctioned path)" — before the case every app
project is actually in. Properly conditional, so not a defect, but it front-loads the path the
customer does not have.
**Proposal.** Reorder so the serial-merge case leads. **Delta.** −30.
